result_text:
Durations under 1 second now round up to `"1s"` instead of becoming `""`. So `step.sleep("id", 500)` gets an op named `"1s"`, and a 500 ms `waitForEvent` timeout becomes `"1s"`.

The existing unit tests and the type check pass, and Biome reformatted the files I touched. I did not add new tests for the round-up or the once-per-process warning. I also did not run a real server to confirm the roughly 1 second sleep and timeout.

- **`timeStr` rounding:** in `helpers/strings.ts`, any value above 0 ms and below 1000 ms becomes 1000 ms before it is split into units. Longer durations still round down, and zero, negative, `Date` and absolute Temporal inputs are unchanged.
- **Warning:** `timeStr(input, logger?)` calls `logger.warn({ requestedMs }, "Durable waits have a minimum resolution of 1s; durations under 1s round up to 1s")` the first time a round-up happens. It never warns again in that process. Because the flag is process-wide, the warning is spent even if no logger was passed on that first round-up.
- **Call sites:** sleep, `waitForEvent`, `waitForSignal`, invoke timeouts and `cancelOn` timeouts all pass `client[internalLoggerSymbol]`. The sleep, `waitForEvent` and invoke ones are in `InngestStepTools.ts`, and `cancelOn` is in `InngestFunction.ts`.
- **JSDoc:** the sleep duration and the `timeout` options now say that durations under 1 second round up to `1s`, the minimum resolution of a durable wait. This covers `types.ts` and `InngestStepTools.ts`.

I left one `timeStr` call alone: `components/middleware/manager.ts:154` uses it only to build a display name for a step, not to send a duration to the server. It therefore doesn't log, though a sub-second value there will show as `"1s"`.
